explanation: Joseph Mohr wrote the words and Franz Xaver Gruber the tune for a Christmas Eve service in the village of Oberndorf. At first it was sung with just a guitar.

claims.text: Silent Night was first performed on Christmas Eve 1818 in Oberndorf, in what is modern Austria.
The premiere of Silent Night did not take place in Germany, Switzerland or Italy.
Joseph Mohr wrote the words of Silent Night and Franz Xaver Gruber composed the tune.
At its first performance Silent Night was accompanied by a guitar.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: clean under content:check for writer w-pmusic01w. Claims: every checkable statement in the stem, options and explanation is listed, with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a fact is beyond everyday knowledge. Datasets: geonames-cities places Oberndorf bei Salzburg in Austria (country AT, admin1 05, Salzburg, 47.93911, 12.95108), which supports the 'modern Austria' part of c1; the premiere itself needs a web source. I used no WebSearch. Rival test: argued for Germany, since the carol's original words, Stille Nacht, are German, which is the trap; Oberndorf is in Austria, so the key stands. The stem says 'modern country' to avoid any argument about the borders of 1818. Volatility: evergreen; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: the carol is sung in hundreds of languages, and the German-language trap works everywhere. Style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words. Myths: screened against myths.json, no hit. Mystery: not applicable to a practice item. Encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: The popular story that the church organ was broken is unproven, so the explanation says only that a guitar was used.
